deities: Sri Ranganathaswamy / Ranganayakulu (presiding deity; Lord Vishnu in the reclining Anantha-Sayana posture on the serpent Adisesha)
Vishnu Sahasranamavali inscribed on the sanctum walls; sacred tank Surya Pushkarini within the premises
festivals: Annual Brahmotsavam (nine days in March-April, with Rathotsavam/chariot procession and fireworks)
Munivahana Utsavam (observed at the temple; verify schedule)

history.dynasty: Pallavas (foundations, 7th c.); Cholas — King Raja Mahendra Varma (12th c.); Vijayanagara emperors (14th-16th c. expansions incl. gopurams and the Nurukalla 100-pillared Mandapam); Aravidu dynasty; Nayakas (17th c.)
history.period: Medieval; foundations attributed to the 7th century, temple constructed/rebuilt in the 12th century
history.summary: The Talpagiri Ranganadhaswamy Temple on the banks of the Penna River is one of the oldest temples in Nellore. Tradition traces its founding to the Pallavas in the 7th century and its construction to King Raja Mahendra Varma in the 12th century; its institutional zenith came under Vijayanagara patronage (14th-16th c.), which added the monumental gopurams and the Nurukalla (100-pillared) Mandapam, with later grants from the Aravidu dynasty and the Nayakas. Its landmark is the Gaaligopuram ('wind tower'), about 70 ft high with gold-plated kalashams, built by Yeragudipati Venkatachalam Panthulu. The temple has a mirror house (a popular devotee attraction), distinct south-facing Rajyalakshmi and north-facing Andal shrines, and the Surya Pushkarini tank. NOTE: Wikipedia's infobox gives coordinates ~14.8788, 79.2979, which place the point ~45 km away from Nellore city; the geocoder POI (Talpagiri Ranganadhaswamy Temple, Ranganayakulapet, Nellore 524001) and the temple's own listed coordinates (~14.4658, 79.9857) agree on the city location, which is used here.

name: Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple
town_description: Nellore is a major city in the Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore district of coastal Andhra Pradesh, on the banks of the Penna River near the Bay of Bengal. It is an old trading and administrative centre known for its temples (Ranganatha, Narasimha Konda), the Nelapattu bird sanctuary nearby, and its spicy Nellore cuisine.

travel.airport: Nearest major airports are Tirupati (~130 km) and Chennai (~175 km) (verify distances).
travel.railway: Nellore railway station (NLR) on the Chennai-Vijayawada main line; the temple is at Ranganayakulapet within the city, a short auto/taxi ride away.
travel.road: Within Nellore city on the banks of the Penna River; well connected by NH-16 and APSRTC buses from Chennai, Vijayawada and Tirupati.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. The annual Brahmotsavam (March-April) is the biggest festival; evenings by the Penna river are considered the most scenic time to visit.
visitor_information.opening_hours: One source lists 6:00 AM to 9:00 PM daily; another lists dawn to dusk (6 AM-6 PM) (conflict — verify on site). Entry is free.
